messages:
Asha (People Ops): Hi team — quick thread about Eli's conversion from TN contractor -> FTE. Need to lock down benefits effective date and payroll start relative to his work authorization timing.
Liam (Hiring Manager): He accepted offer last week, start date on offer is June 1. Eli's TN entry was originally as contractor and he plans to switch at US border the week before start.
Marina (Immigration Specialist): TL;DR: TN-to-FTE at border is fine but depends on what Eli presents at POE. If they admit him in TN status, we technically can start him, but for certain benefits and payroll we need SSN and I-9 completion.
Eli (New hire): Confirming I plan to cross on May 28 and present TN docs with updated LCA/offer letter. I don't yet have SSN — applied but card may be delayed.
Asha (People Ops): Thanks Eli. Two parallel checks: payroll needs I-9 complete + either SSN or SSN pending note for payroll tax setup; benefits (medical/401k) typically enroll on first of month after hire or effective date depending on plan. We need to decide if we make benefits effective June 1 or delay until SSN on file.
Liam (Hiring Manager): We want him covered from day one. Is there a way to provisionally enroll him and then update SSN later?
Marina (Immigration Specialist): From immigration side nothing blocks day-one work once admitted. For SSN: he can start work and apply; the SSN card issuance is independent.
Asha (People Ops): Insurance vendor allows provisional enrollment if employee has pending SSN, but payroll & tax withholding prefer SSN on record. Payroll Bot: FYI — without SSN we set a placeholder and employees may be put on statutory withholding until SSN is provided, which could cause retroactive adjustments.
Eli (New hire): I can bring a receipt of SSN application and my passport + TN docs to I-9. Would that let HR verify identity for now?
Marina (Immigration Specialist): For I-9, acceptable documents are passport + TN admission stamp (or Form I-94). Receipt of SSN application is NOT an I-9 acceptable doc. But for benefits vendor provisional enrollment, proof of application often works.
Asha (People Ops): Plan proposal: 1) Proceed with start date June 1. 2) Complete I-9 on day one with passport + I-94. 3) Enroll Eli in benefits effective June 1 provisionally (we need a signed benefits waiver if he opts out). 4) Payroll will run on next cycle; Payroll Bot will create a placeholder SSN entry and update when Eli provides his card to payroll@redwood.com. Any retro tax adjustments will be handled via payroll reconciliation.
Liam (Hiring Manager): OK with me — can People Ops confirm with payroll vendor about retro adjustments and provide a note in the offer pack so candidate understands potential short-term paycheck differences?
Asha (People Ops): Yep. I'll add a short clause to the offer addendum about SSN timing and potential retro changes. Also will create a checklist for Eli: border admission docs, I-94 print, SSN application receipt, signed W-4, benefits forms.
Marina (Immigration Specialist): Also note: if POE officer denies TN entry for any reason (rare), we need backup: either deferred start or remote start from Canada if role permits. Liam, please confirm remote option in contingency plan?
Liam (Hiring Manager): We can do remote for up to 2 weeks if needed. I'll update hiring doc.
Eli (New hire): Thanks all — I'll share my SSN receipt and I-94 to the secure HR upload link once I have them. Any special filename or suffix?
Asha (People Ops): Use: elihn_ssn_receipt_YYYYMMDD.pdf and elihn_i94_YYYYMMDD.pdf and upload to the secure portal. We'll email you a prefilled benefits packet today.
Payroll Bot: Reminder: new hire setup form required by payroll@redwood.com before first payroll run.
Asha (People Ops): I'll hit payroll and immigration vendor (Marina) after this thread to confirm vendor-side flags and to request priority processing if SSN card delayed. Closing: action items listed in thread + I'll post a one-pager in #onboarding-ops with the checklist. :white_check_mark:
